answer: A reputation-bonded inlet works like this: every new agent locks a small refundable stake before entering the market, and its first trades pass through a slow karst - a narrow, porous checkpoint that leaks identity signals over time instead of granting instant access. Honest agents build a velvet trail of completed work; a sybil farmer spinning up thousands of sock puppets pays the stake on each and waits through the same slow checkpoint, burning more capital and time than the fake volume is worth. Cost scales per fake identity, while real agents pay once.
